slides.0.title: Sherry
slides.0.subtitle: One grape, one soil, and a whole family of styles from maturation alone
slides.1.title: Terroir and varieties
slides.1.highlights.0.title: The triangle
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Jerez de la Frontera, El Puerto de Santa María and Sanlúcar de Barrameda form the ageing triangle; southern Spain is hot, but the humid Atlantic westerly (poniente) moderates it
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Albariza soil
slides.1.highlights.1.content: White, calcium-rich soil that soaks up winter rain and forms a crust in summer that limits evaporation, giving vines water through the hot, dry summer
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Varieties
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Neutral, low-acid Palomino is the basis of dry Sherry; Pedro Ximénez (PX) and Moscatel are often sun-dried (asoleo) to make intensely sweet wines, also used for sweetening
slides.1.content: Palomino’s neutrality is exactly what lets maturation take the lead in style.
slides.2.title: The family of styles
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Fino and Manzanilla
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Fortified to about 15–15.5% and aged biologically under flor: pale, dry, almond and dough; Manzanilla must age in Sanlúcar, where sea humidity thickens the flor for a fresher, saltier style
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Oloroso
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Fortified to about 17% or more, so flor cannot survive; purely oxidative: deep amber, nuts, leather and toffee, and naturally dry
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Amontillado and Palo Cortado
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Amontillado ages first under flor and then oxidatively once the flor dies, combining both characters; Palo Cortado has Amontillado-like finesse on the nose and Oloroso-like body
slides.2.content: The strength of fortification decides whether flor survives, and so the style.
slides.3.title: Sweet styles, age statements and market
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Sweet Sherry
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Naturally sweet styles are PX and Moscatel; sweetened blends (Pale Cream, Medium, Cream) mix dry Sherry with PX or concentrated must, are affordable and sell in volume in traditional export markets
slides.3.highlights.1.title: VOS and VORS
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Officially certified average ages after tasting and analysis: VOS at least 20 years, VORS at least 30; there are also 12- and 15-year age statements
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Market and new trends
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Traditional sweet exports have long been declining; recently en rama (lightly filtered Fino), single-vineyard and old age-dated Sherries attract restaurants and sommeliers, moving towards smaller volumes at higher value
slides.3.content: Sherry industry questions: volume sweet styles are shrinking; premium dry and old wines are the way forward.
